podcast.body: This song was a huge pop hit in 1976, but its overtly sexual nature led some radio stations to refuse to play it. "I mean Rod Stewart has this smash hit that some radio stations would not play because it is so overtly sexual."

srcs.episode: Ep. 31 - The Spirit of '76 - Pop Music on America's Bicentennial

podcast.body: This "shambling seduction slow jam" was the Billboard year-end number one for 1977, topping the Hot 100 for eight weeks starting in late 1976. Despite being a "silly song" with an "infamous lyric" that is considered "a little gross," it surprisingly beat out other strong contenders for the year-end title. "I doubt you would have guessed tonight's the night a shambling seduction slow jam which top the hot 100 for eight weeks starting in late 1976 and took the title for 77."
